steps.title: Where it sits
steps.caption: Acme Shop writes to PostgreSQL; CDC through Kafka feeds the products index; searches go there.
steps.body: Acme Shop keeps its catalogue in **PostgreSQL**, the system of record. Debezium reads each committed change and publishes it to the Kafka topic `acme.public.products`, and **search-indexer** writes it to the index **products** with the `_bulk` API. The app sends its searches here instead of to the database and gets ranked hits with brand counts; the same engine also serves log analytics, with logs kept in data streams.

steps.title: Analyse, index, refresh
steps.caption: Red ceramic mug is analysed into red, ceram, mug; a refresh 1 s later makes it searchable in P1.
steps.body: The `english` analyzer splits *Red ceramic mug* into tokens, lower-cases them and stems them to the terms **red**, **ceram** and **mug**, and the **inverted index** lists, for each term, the documents that contain it. The write lands in an in-memory buffer and the **translog**, which is fsynced before the write is acknowledged. A **refresh**, every second here, turns the buffer into a new segment that search can see (near real time), and small segments are merged in the background.

steps.title: Route, replicate, search
steps.caption: _id 14 routes to P1, which copies it to R1. node-1 asks one copy of each shard, merges, fetches 3.
steps.body: The `_bulk` request reaches node-3, and `hash(_id) % 3` sends document `14` to shard 1: primary **P1** on node-2 indexes it and forwards it to replica **R1** on node-3, and only then is the write acknowledged. The search for *red mug* reaches **node-1**, which sends it to one copy of every shard (R0, R1 and P2 here); each returns its top hits with scores and its brand counts, and node-1 merges them, fetches the 3 winning documents and answers.

steps.title: Failover and the limits
steps.caption: node-2 fails: R1 becomes primary, health turns yellow. Limits: a copy, mappings, paging, shards.
steps.body: **node-2** fails. The master promotes **R1** on node-3 to primary, searches and writes go on, and the cluster health is **yellow** until the missing replicas are rebuilt, which by default starts after 1 minute. The limits: the index is a derived copy that lags by the refresh interval and has no multi-document transactions, uncontrolled field names can blow up the mapping, deep pages with `from` and `size` are expensive, and the shard count is fixed when the index is created.
